analysis.title: GS Crook - GS MORNING 1) Japanese Portfolio Flows, 2) Waller Comments, 3) Asia Equities Update and 4) 5 Key Charts 9 Oct 2026
key_insights: GS FX Research (Fishman) recently turned structurally bullish Yen. The BoJ appears to be hiking faster, and the government appears to be encouraging domestic investors to reallocate toward domestic assets.

September ITS data show no sign of rotation among mostly unhedged Japanese investors. Trust accounts (which include the public pension fund) bought $7.6bn of foreign bonds vs $14.7bn in August and a six-month average of $8.6bn. Investment trusts (retail/NISA) bought $8.7bn of foreign equities vs $8.5bn in August.

Typically hedged Japanese investors are repatriating. Banks' net sales of foreign bonds rose from $8.3bn in August to $15.9bn in September. Lifers net sold $1.9bn vs $0.9bn. Total 12-month flows look increasingly negative, similar to the 2022 period of rising global yields.
The ITS data predate the past week's sudden volatility in the European bond market. France is the largest share of Japan's foreign debt holdings after the US.

Fed Governor Waller expects about two more rate hikes if data come in as expected. He said they need not come at consecutive meetings. He cited the unresolved Middle East conflict, AI buildout raising consumer prices for technology goods, and tariff risk as reasons for less confidence that inflation is returning to 2%.

GS US Economics (Mericle) still expects one more 25bp hike in December. It has lowered the probability that the FOMC passes on a December hike, because Waller's speech is more hawkish than his earlier emphasis on the 3-month annualized core PCE rate, now 2.0%.

GS FX Strategy (Jenkins) says the USD rally rests on three drivers: rate differentials, relative equity/tech outperformance, and Brent back above $100. Only energy and AI look structural, while Fed pricing is the shakiest. GS is the most dovish in G10 versus market pricing, alongside the BoE.

Jenkins thinks EUR may have run ahead of fundamentals and that USDJPY has structural downside asymmetry, so it is early to press USD strength. GS Econ's call is a hold in October and a hike in December.

GS Asia Portfolio Strategy (Moe) stays positive on Asia, focused on tech-driven earnings. Regional earnings are forecast to grow 34% over 2026-2028, with info tech at a 20% CAGR over five years on AI compute demand.

Moe raised the 10-year MXAPJ annual earnings growth forecast by 1pp to 10%. GS sees 16% valuation upside for hard tech, 3% for non-tech and 10% for MXAPJ overall at 11.3x P/E. It forecasts a 26% 12-month USD price return and a 14% 10-year average annual USD total return.

MXAPJ composition has shifted. Taiwan is 29% of the index and Korea 22%, together half. China fell from a 40%+ peak in late 2020 to 19%, and India from 19% to 10%. Info tech is 43% of index cap, ahead of financials.
Concentration in MXAPJ is at a record. The top 10 stocks are 41% of regional cap, 4.0 s.d. above the long-term mean of about 24%. TSMC, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix alone are 29%.
GS's Brent fair value model implies a $22/bbl average risk premium in September, the second-highest monthly risk premium on record.
The generic congressional ballot has increasingly favoured Democrats.
Taiwan exports show sustained strength, led by information, communication and audiovisual products.
The S&P 500 and S&P ex-AI have diverged by a 10% spread in 5 weeks.

sector_views.rationale: AI-driven compute demand underpins a 20% earnings CAGR over five years, with an estimated 16% valuation upside for hard tech.
GS estimates only 3% valuation upside for non-tech, though it flags non-tech earnings compounders as a key theme.

earnings_insights: GS forecasts MXAPJ earnings growth of 75% in 2026, 25% in 2027 and 14% in 2028 (GS forecasts, in line with consensus but with meaningful variation by market). Cumulative growth is 34% over 2026-2028 per the report's headline figure.

macro_indicators.reading: One additional 25bp hike expected in December
macro_indicators.interpretation: GS has lowered the probability that the FOMC skips a December hike after Waller's hawkish speech. GS still expects a hold in October.
Waller had previously emphasized this rate. His latest speech shifted toward flagging further hikes despite it.
Waller said the hikes need not come at consecutive meetings but should be in place within an acceptable period. This is a hawkish shift.
Brent back above $100 is one of the three legs of the USD rally. GS sees energy as a structural driver.
This is the second-highest monthly risk premium on record in GS's Brent fair value model.

trade_ideas.rationale: Domestic policies that weighed on the currency are shifting, with faster BoJ hikes and government encouragement of reallocation toward domestic assets.
trade_ideas.risk: Flows have not yet rotated among unhedged investors, and any shift is expected to be slow-moving.

trade_ideas.rationale: All three USD drivers have been mean-reverting this year, and USDJPY has structural downside asymmetry.

trade_ideas.description: Positive on Asia ex-Japan equities, focused on tech-driven North Asia (Taiwan, Korea) with selected diversification
trade_ideas.rationale: Regional earnings are forecast to grow 34% from 2026-2028, led by tech, with a 26% 12-month USD price return forecast for MXAPJ.
trade_ideas.risk: Record index concentration, with the top 10 stocks at 41% of cap.
